roles.title: Intent
roles.mission: Spell out the one-line requirement: for whom, why, and what counts as success
roles.brief: First look up in the knowledge base "Larkspur Outfitters" the standards and data the task lists, then read the "Requirement" section at the end of the README and `.kiro/steering/` (this is the company web template: the server skeleton, page shell and brand styles already exist). Write `docs/aidlc/1-ideation/intent.md`: for whom, why, what success looks like (each point verifiable), and what is not in scope this time; say which knowledge base document holds the data the requirement needs. One page at most, no code.

roles.title: Constraints
roles.mission: Check against the company standards: which ones apply this time, and where the requirement conflicts with them
roles.brief: In the knowledge base "Larkspur Outfitters", look up each company standard the task lists, and go through its rule IDs (PII-n, FE-n, BR-n, ACC-n, ...): does the rule apply this time, and why. Write `docs/aidlc/1-ideation/constraints.md`: the rules that apply (ID + one sentence on how to meet it); one line for each that does not; and last a separate section "For a person to decide": where the requirement's own words conflict with a rule, and the consequences of each way out. Do not decide a conflict for the person, and do not quietly go one way. One page at most, no code.

roles.title: Scope
roles.mission: Combine intent and constraints into one scope list for a person to approve
roles.brief: Read `docs/aidlc/1-ideation/intent.md` and `constraints.md` and write `docs/aidlc/1-ideation/scope.md`: the list of items to build this time, each with an ID AC-n, one sentence on what to build, and which company rule it answers (give the ID); what is explicitly not built; and the items under "For a person to decide" in `constraints.md`, copied as they are, with how you suggest deciding each and why. Keep the list short and exact: fewer items is better than vague ones. Then write the delivery tag `docs/aidlc/1-ideation/delivery.json`: one JSON object with the keys name (the delivery's name, at most 16 characters), kind (new app, new feature or fix), size (small, medium or large), line (e-commerce, mobile apps, CRM, supply chain or internal systems) and why (one sentence); it counts in the company's delivery statistics. Also write what is for a person to decide as `docs/aidlc/1-ideation/questions.json`: `{"questions": [{"id": "1", "q": "a one-sentence question", "options": [{"key": "A", "text": "the option and its cost"}, {"key": "B", "text": "..."}], "recommend": "A", "why": "one sentence of reasons"}]}`, with ids matching the numbers in the document, 2 to 4 options per question, and recommend naming the option you suggest; if nothing is for a person to decide write `{"questions": []}`. The person chooses one by one at the gate; what they choose is final and is handed to every later role. When you are done the run stops for a person's approval; the person may delete or change items or settle how a conflict is handled, and the person's word wins.

roles.title: Architect
roles.mission: Define the interfaces and the shape of the pages, and give the development roles their directories
roles.brief: Read the scope list (where a person's approval note differs, the person's wins) and the README's "Company template conventions" section. Write `docs/aidlc/2-inception/architecture.md` (which pages, which endpoints, which data, which file under `server/data/` the data is copied to from the knowledge base, and where each item of the scope list lands) and `interfaces.md` (for each endpoint: method, path, request, success and error responses; for each page: the page name, the shape of the `render(state)` state, and the `data-*` attributes the tests need). Then write the assignment file `docs/aidlc/2-inception/ownership.json` in this format: `{"roles": {"backend": ["server/routes/**", "server/data/**"], "frontend": ["web/pages/**", "web/styles/**", "web/motion/**"], "mobile": []}, "test_areas": {"server": "backend", "web": "frontend"}}`. In roles use only the keys backend, frontend and mobile, each with the directories it may change; this template has no Android app, so give mobile an empty list (it will be skipped); always write server and web in test_areas (the company checks and the test file names use them to assign work to roles). Write documents only, no code.

roles.title: UI design
roles.mission: Design the pages with the company's components and brand style
roles.brief: First look up the brand standard and the frontend engineering standard in the knowledge base. From the scope list and the pages in `interfaces.md`, write `docs/aidlc/2-inception/design.md`: for each page its layout, which of the site-wide components the README lists it uses, its copy (in the tone BR-5 asks for), and the three states loading, empty and error; use only the brand variables in `tokens.css` for colour. One page at most, no code.

roles.title: Requirements
roles.mission: Write the scope as acceptance criteria, and put the start-phase results together for a person to approve
roles.brief: Read the scope list, `architecture.md`, `interfaces.md`, `ownership.json` and `design.md`, and write `docs/aidlc/2-inception/acceptance.md`: write each item of the scope as an acceptance criterion (keep the AC-n IDs), say how to verify it (which endpoint to call, what to look at on the page) and which company rule it answers; say whether a machine checks it or a person looks. Every note a person added at a gate must have an acceptance criterion. One page at most. Then collect what a person has to decide from the inception stage (architecture, interfaces, assignment, design and your acceptance criteria): the items earlier documents marked "for a person to decide" or "to be confirmed", and the conflicts you found, into `docs/aidlc/2-inception/questions.json`: `{"questions": [{"id": "1", "q": "a one-sentence question", "options": [{"key": "A", "text": "the option and its cost"}, {"key": "B", "text": "..."}], "recommend": "A", "why": "one sentence of reasons"}]}`, with ids matching the numbers in the document, 2 to 4 options per question, and recommend naming the option you suggest; if nothing is for a person to decide write `{"questions": []}`. The person chooses one by one at the gate; what they choose is final and is handed to every later role. When you are done the run stops: at the "Build start" gate the person reads all the documents of this stage and approves, and only then do the code and the checks start.

roles.title: Compliance & security
roles.mission: Turn the company rules that apply to the scope into checks a machine can judge: red first, then green
roles.brief: Read `constraints.md`, the scope list (a person's approval note wins) and `interfaces.md`, and look up the original text of the standards that apply in the knowledge base. `tests/enterprise/` already holds the checks the company issues (see its README and file names: FE-1/2/4, UX-2, BR-1 and PII-1 are already covered), so do not write those again. Write the remaining applicable rules that a machine can judge as checks `tests/comp-<area>-<topic>.test.js` (take the area name from test_areas in ownership.json: server or web; ES modules, `node:test`; for endpoints use `startServer` from `tests/enterprise/_lib.js` and call `close()` when done; for pages import and call `render` directly), starting each test name with the rule ID, six tests at most. The implementation is not written yet, so red is correct. Then write one page `docs/aidlc/3-construction/compliance.md`: which check covers each applicable rule, and which rules only a person can judge. When you are done run `node tests/enterprise/_run.cjs comp-` to confirm they run (red is fine).

roles.title: Testing
roles.mission: Write tests from the acceptance criteria
roles.brief: Write tests from `acceptance.md` and `interfaces.md` as `tests/ac-<area>-<topic>.test.js` (take the area name from test_areas in ownership.json: server or web; ES modules, `node:test`; for endpoints use `startServer` from `tests/enterprise/_lib.js`, start one per case and call `close()` in `finally`; for pages import `web/pages/<page name>.js` and call `render(state)`). Pick the most important ACs, one test each, starting the test name with the AC number, twelve tests at most; every note a person added at a gate must be covered. The implementation is not written yet, so red is correct; do not write an implementation to check your tests. When you are done run `node tests/enterprise/_run.cjs ac-` to confirm they run, then commit.

roles.title: Backend
roles.brief: Implement the endpoints in `server/routes/` as `interfaces.md` says (the format is in the note at the top of `server/routes/index.js`); take the data you need from the knowledge base and copy it unchanged into `server/data/`, at the path the knowledge base's description document gives (use `cp`, do not change the content). Look up the standards the task lists in the knowledge base, and put the rule IDs in code comments and commit messages. Fix the checks whose file names put them in your area (server): `tests/enterprise/*-server-*`, `tests/comp-server-*`, `tests/ac-server-*`. When you are done run `node tests/enterprise/_run.cjs server-` to confirm they are all green.

roles.title: Web
roles.brief: Write the pages `web/pages/<page name>.js` (`render` / `mount`, see the README's "Page conventions") and `web/styles/<page name>.css` as `interfaces.md` and `design.md` say, and register them in `web/pages/index.js`; you may replace the template's placeholder home page. Use the site-wide components the README lists, use only the variables in `tokens.css` for colour, and show personal data as the personal data display standard says. Fix the checks whose file names put them in your area (web): `tests/enterprise/*-web-*`, `tests/comp-web-*`, `tests/ac-web-*`. When you are done run `node tests/enterprise/_run.cjs web-` to confirm they are all green.

roles.title: Android
roles.mission: The Android app (starts only if the assignment gives it directories)
roles.brief: Work only in the directories the assignment file gives you; call the endpoints as `interfaces.md` says, and show personal data as the personal data display standard says. Fix the checks whose file names put them in your area.

roles.title: Review
roles.mission: Independent and read-only; checks item by item and sends work back if it needs changes
roles.brief: You took no part in the development; you look at the result only. First look up in the knowledge base the standards the task lists, then read the scope list (where a person's approval note differs, the person's wins), `acceptance.md` and `git diff` (the command is below). Check item by item: whether each item of the scope is done, whether the company rules that apply are met (personal data, frontend engineering, brand), and count the tests that fail on the test wall into your verdict. On the first line of your reply write `DONE: ready to deliver` or `DONE: changes needed: <one sentence>`. Below it, number each issue that needs a change separately as F-1, F-2, ...: which rule it breaks, the file and line, the evidence (the code itself), how to fix it, and who owns it (write a line such as `Send back: Backend`); when you let it through, also list 2 or 3 "non-blocking risk notes". What a person decided in the scope is not a problem. The owner will read your report at the release gate and decide whether to approve the release or send it back.

roles.title: Deploy
roles.brief: Write the deployment config `deploy/local.json`: `{ "port": 8085, "health": "/" }` (the port and the health check path; if there are endpoints, the health check may be a GET endpoint that takes no parameters), and a one-page deployment record `docs/aidlc/4-operation/deploy.md`: how to start, the health check, and rollback (stop the process, go back to the previous commit). Smoke-test once on a free port: `PORT=18085 node server/server.js &`, and when `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 127.0.0.1:18085/` returns 200, stop it. Do not use 8085: after you commit, the pipeline (the orchestrator) deploys with your config to 127.0.0.1:8085, and the deployment counts as successful only when the health check returns 200; if it fails, the reason is sent back to you.

roles.title: Lessons
roles.mission: List the lessons from this delivery worth keeping for next time, for a person to tick
roles.brief: Read `docs/aidlc/decisions.md` (what the person said and decided at each gate), the issues numbered F-n in the review's report, and why work was sent back this time (see the `[run]` commits in `git log`). Pick the lessons worth passing on to the next delivery, each one sentence that can be followed directly; use the person's own words where you can, and do not rewrite them into stock phrases. If nothing is worth keeping, list none: do not pad. Write `docs/aidlc/5-knowledge/questions.json`: `{"questions": [{"id": "1", "q": "Which lessons from this delivery should be remembered? Ticked ones are saved and read by every later run; unticked ones are not kept.", "multi": true, "options": [{"key": "A", "text": "one lesson"}, ...], "why": "unticked means not kept"}]}`, at most 10 lessons, each at most 200 characters. When there are no candidates, write an empty array for `questions`. Do not change any other file.
